question: Semantics of lookup stub 0x007B6C30 (region 0x007B6C30-0x007B6C4B): pure property lookup vs get-or-create/register; what it does with key 0x00A85460 and receivers [elem]/[elem+0x24]; jump target VA if any

claims.statement: Structure census of the admitted region: exactly 14 instruction rows (0x007b6c30-0x007b6c48, listing lines 959600-959613), single logical function with entry 0x007B6C30, 0 CALL sites in-region, 2 control-flow edges out of the window (E1: conditional JNZ to 0x007B6C4B; E2: fall-through epilogue to normal return via RET 0x4), 3 callee-saved register PUSH/POP pairs (EBX,EBP,EDI), and ZERO memory writes (the only stack writes are the 3 register saves; no store to receiver, globals, or any keyed table).
claims.evidence: EXTRACT_007B6C30_REGION.txt rows 959600-959613 (verbatim, SHA 40516D35...7A3C); single-entry structure supported by 32 direct CALL rows in the saved listing targeting 0x007b6c30 (address-index navigation census).
premises: pinned saved-listing fidelity for this region
direct CALL target implies function entry (address-index navigation, not ABI proof)
claims.countermodel: mis-decompiled listing row (would falsify all row-level claims); none observable in-region; listing is the frozen pinned source, not re-derived.

claims.statement: Calling convention (arithmetic-derived, in-region): thiscall - receiver/this arrives in ECX (MOV EBP,ECX @0x007b6c33 after saving caller EBP); exactly ONE by-value DWORD stack argument (the key), located at [ESP+0x10] after the 3 PUSHes (CMP dword ptr [ESP+0x10],EBX @0x007b6c3d), and popped by the callee via RET 0x4 @0x007b6c48. Stack-balance derivation: entry [ESP]=retaddr,[ESP+4]=key; +3 pushes => key at [ESP+0x10]. Epilogue POPs restore EDI,EBP,EBX in reverse order; XOR EAX,EAX sets NULL return before final POP/RET.
claims.evidence: EXTRACT rows 959600-959613; per-instruction stack arithmetic (MEMORY_AND_IDENTITY.json stack map).
premises: MSVC-style thiscall for ECX-receiver + callee-pops-one-DWORD (RET 0x4) shape
claims.countermodel: a second stack argument hidden below the first would break the [ESP+0x10] identification; refuted by RET 0x4 popping exactly 4 bytes (one DWORD) - the epilogue is stack-balanced against a single 4-byte argument.

claims.statement: Null-key fast path: if key==0, the function returns EAX=0 (NULL) immediately via the in-region epilogue, with NO table access, NO create, NO receiver write. The receiver member [this+0x18] is dereferenced UNCONDITIONALLY BEFORE the key test (MOV EDI,[EBP+0x18] @0x007b6c35 precedes CMP @0x007b6c3d), so even a null-key call requires a valid receiver object (caller must pass non-null, at least 0x1C-readable receiver; consistent with P02's sentinel-guarded receivers).
premises: instruction order in the listing = execution order on this path (single straight-line block, no other branches in-region)
claims.countermodel: none in-region; the unconditional-load ordering is directly visible.

claims.statement: Receiver member read and register pre-computation: EDI = M[this+0x18] - 1, computed register-only (SUB EDI,0x1 @0x007b6c3a operates on the register copy; NO store back to [this+0x18]). EBX=0 (XOR EBX,EBX). These plus EBP=this are carried LIVE-INTO the continuation at 0x007B6C4B on the non-null-key path.
claims.evidence_level: CONFIRMED (read/sub/zeroing rows) / PLAUSIBLE (continuation actually consumes EDI/EBX)
claims.evidence: EXTRACT rows 959603-959606; register liveness into the JNZ target.
premises: PLAUSIBLE part: a standard optimizing compiler would dead-code-eliminate an unused load+sub, so the continuation uses EDI; this is a compiler-behavior premise, not an in-region fact
claims.countermodel: continuation ignores EDI/EBX (then load+sub would be dead code - unlikely under DCE but not in-region refutable); no claim below depends on the PLAUSIBLE part being true except the hedged interpretation of [this+0x18] as a continuation-consumed count.

claims.statement: Derived per-callsite dispatch: the two P02 leaf-action callsites pass the compile-time constant key 0x00A85460 (cited P02: PUSH 0x00A85460; MOV ECX,EBX; CALL 0x007b6c30, and the [elem+0x24] fallback form). Since 0x00A85460 != 0, the JNZ @0x007b6c41 is ALWAYS TAKEN at those callsites: both lookup calls ALWAYS enter the continuation at 0x007B6C4B. The in-region null-key fast path is DEAD for the P02 leaf action; the entire semantic outcome (lookup result, and any binding write) is produced by the unadmitted continuation.
claims.evidence: EXTRACT rows 959607-959608 (CMP/JNZ); key constant cited from P02 REPORT (P02-C4: key=0x00A85460=0x00A85454+0xC, arithmetic CONFIRMED in P02).
premises: key value at those callsites is the pushed constant (P02 admitted-region fact, cited)
claims.countermodel: key somehow null at those callsites - refuted by the constant PUSH cited from P02's admitted region.

claims.statement: MAIN CLAIM (scoped answer): (a) IN-REGION, 0x007B6C30 is a pure GUARD + IN-FUNCTION DISPATCH, not a registrar: zero memory writes, key passed by value, null key returns NULL - the 14 admitted rows CANNOT write a binding through any channel (no store instruction exists other than register saves). (b) FULL-FUNCTION semantics (pure property lookup vs get-or-create/register) are NOT_ESTABLISHED from the admitted region: the decision lives entirely in the same function's continuation at 0x007B6C4B (jump/fall-through target VA = 0x007B6C4B; single logical function, not a separate callee). A get-or-create/register continuation would write the binding (entry insert + possibly count update at M[this+0x18]) - this countermodel remains live and is exactly P02-B1 unresolved.

claims.evidence: full in-region store census (P03-C1); dispatch analysis (P03-C3, P03-C5); P02 context citation for the countermodel motivation.
